title: Vegetable Stock
desc: Unsalted vegetable stock for soups, grains and sauces.
steps: Heat the oil in a large stockpot over medium heat.
Add onion, carrot, celery, leek, bay, thyme and peppercorns.
Sweat for 8 minutes without browning, then pour in the water.
Simmer gently, uncovered, for 45 minutes. Strain without pressing the vegetables.
Measure the strained stock; reduce gently or add water to reach the displayed yield.
Use immediately or divide into shallow containers, cool promptly and refrigerate within 2 hours.

title: White Chicken Stock
desc: A light, unsalted stock made from unroasted chicken bones.
steps: Place chicken bones and wings in a large stockpot. Cover with the cold water.
Bring slowly to a simmer and skim off foam; do not let it boil hard.
Add onion, carrot, celery, leek, bay, thyme and peppercorns.
Simmer uncovered for 3 hours, keeping the bones submerged with water. Strain and skim off fat.
Measure the strained stock; reduce gently or add water to reach the displayed yield.
Use immediately or divide into shallow containers, cool promptly and refrigerate within 2 hours.

title: Brown Chicken Stock
desc: Roasted bones and vegetables make a rich, unsalted stock.
steps: Preheat to 200°C fan. Spread the bones in a roasting tray and roast for 40 minutes, turning once.
Add onion, carrot, celery and leek. Coat with tomato paste and roast for 15 minutes more.
Transfer to a stockpot. Rinse the browned tray with some of the measured water and add this with the remaining water, bay, thyme and peppercorns.
Simmer gently for 3 hours, skimming foam and topping up water to keep the bones covered. Strain and skim off fat.
Measure the strained stock; reduce gently or add water to reach the displayed yield.
Use immediately or divide into shallow containers, cool promptly and refrigerate within 2 hours.

title: Fish Fumet
desc: A delicate, unsalted white-fish stock for sauces and soups.
steps: Melt the butter in a stockpot. Soften the onion and leek for 5 minutes without colouring.
Add the fish bones and stir gently for 2 minutes. Pour in the wine and simmer for 2 minutes.
Add water, bay and parsley. Simmer very gently for 20 minutes, skimming foam; strain through a fine sieve.
Measure the strained stock; reduce gently or add water to reach the displayed yield.
Use immediately or divide into shallow containers, cool promptly and refrigerate within 2 hours.

title: Court Bouillon
desc: An aromatic poaching liquid for fish.
steps: Put water, wine and vinegar into a wide saucepan.
Add onion, carrot, celery, bay, peppercorns and salt.
Simmer for 25 minutes, then strain.
Measure the strained stock; reduce gently or add water to reach the displayed yield.
Use as a poaching liquid; bring back to a gentle simmer before adding fish.

title: White Veal Stock
desc: Unroasted veal bones make a light, unsalted stock for white sauces.
steps: Put veal bones in a large stockpot and cover with the cold water.
Bring slowly to a simmer and skim off foam; do not let it boil hard.
Add onion, carrot, celery, leek, bay, thyme and peppercorns.
Simmer for 5 hours, adding water to keep the bones covered. Strain and skim off fat.
Measure the strained stock; reduce gently or add water to reach the displayed yield.
Use immediately or divide into shallow containers, cool promptly and refrigerate within 2 hours.

title: Roasting Jus
desc: A light roasting jus without flour.
steps: Pour the defatted roasting juices into a small saucepan.
Add red wine and simmer for 5 minutes.
Stir in the prepared brown beef stock and simmer until concentrated, about 15 minutes.
Measure the strained stock; reduce gently or add water to reach the displayed yield.

title: Meat Glaze
desc: Unsalted brown stock reduced to a concentrated glaze.
steps: Pour the prepared brown beef stock into a wide saucepan.
Simmer uncovered, skimming any foam, until thick and syrupy; allow 60–90 minutes.
Lower the heat as it thickens and stir frequently to prevent scorching.
Measure the strained stock; reduce gently or add water to reach the displayed yield.
Use immediately or divide into shallow containers, cool promptly and refrigerate within 2 hours.
